title: Unraveling the allosteric mechanism and mechanical stability of partial and complete loss-of-function mutations in p53 DNA-binding domain.
authors: Zhou, Han; Zhou, Tao; Yan, Shiwei
one_liner_zh: 该文通过全原子MD和拉伸模拟研究p53 DNA结合域突变对二聚体-DNA复合物动态互作与机械稳定性的别构机制，核心聚焦TF-DNA结合体系，方法为物理模拟，高度匹配课题。
abstract: Mutations in functional proteins are the core cause of protein misfolding and dysfunction. Different mutation types exert distinct effects on protein structure and function, thus determining the specificity and diversity of targeted therapeutic strategies. In this study, we took the tumor suppressor protein p53 as a model to investigate the impacts of different mutation types on protein structure and function. Mutations in the p53 protein primarily occur in its DNA-binding domain (p53-DBD), and such mutations are classified into hotspot mutations (causing complete loss-of-function) and non-hotspot mutations (inducing partial loss-of-function). However, the allosteric mechanisms underlying non-hotspot mutations remain elusive. We conducted all-atom molecular dynamics simulations for the three systems: p53-WT, non-hotspot p53-E180R, and hotspot p53-R248W dimer-DNA complexes. Our results demonstrate that both mutations weaken intramolecular interactions in p53-DBD and enhance its structural flexibility. In particular, E180R perturbs dimer interface interactions, impairing dimer stability and cooperative DNA binding; R248W disrupts interactions between the L3/L1 loops and DNA, leading to the loss of DNA-binding capacity. These allosteric effects agree with available experimental data. Steered molecular dynamics simulations further confirm that both mutations accelerate p53 dimer dissociation. We also reveal for the first time the mechanical stability features of intermolecular interactions within p53 dimers. These findings provide atomic-level insights into p53 mutation-associated allostery and offer a basis for distinguishing mutation subtypes in prognosis prediction and targeted therapeutic strategy design.
abstract_zh: 功能蛋白的突变是蛋白质错误折叠和功能障碍的核心原因。不同类型的突变对蛋白质结构和功能产生不同影响，从而决定了靶向治疗策略的特异性和多样性。本研究以肿瘤抑制蛋白p53为模型，探讨不同突变类型对蛋白质结构和功能的影响。p53蛋白的突变主要发生在其DNA结合域（p53-DBD）中，此类突变分为热点突变（导致完全功能丧失）和非热点突变（引起部分功能丧失）。然而，非热点突变背后的变构机制仍不明确。我们对p53-WT、非热点p53-E180R和热点p53-R248W二聚体-DNA复合物三个系统进行了全原子分子动力学模拟。结果表明，两种突变均削弱了p53-DBD中的分子内相互作用，并增强了其结构灵活性。特别地，E180R扰乱了二聚体界面相互作用，损害了二聚体稳定性和协同DNA结合能力；R248W破坏了L3/L1环与DNA之间的相互作用，导致DNA结合能力丧失。这些变构效应与现有实验数据一致。拉伸分子动力学模拟进一步证实，两种突变均加速了p53二聚体解离。我们还首次揭示了p53二聚体内分子间相互作用的机械稳定性特征。这些发现为p53突变相关变构提供了原子级见解，并为预后预测和靶向治疗策略设计中区分突变亚型提供了基础。
